title: Command palette (ctrl+p)
brief: Command palette of goop, opened with ctrl+p and restyled after a Linux app launcher (walker/anyrun). A centered ~600px box on --background-panel with a 1px --text-muted border on all four sides (bordered like every modal box; no radius, no shadow) sits over the dimmed, inert 04 session; the composer edge turns --border. Inside: no title, no esc label, no hint row. The search line shows a lavender cursor and the muted placeholder search commands. Below it a flat list of 10 rows about two lines high, no category headers: a 2-cell icon tile filled with the command's meaning color (--success offers, --secondary search and sources, --accent rules and profile, --primary agents and models, --text-muted session, settings, privacy and help, --error quit; never lavender) with a Nerd Font glyph in --background, two spaces, then the label at the 15px normal role. The selected row's label is bold --primary and only that row shows its keybind or slash command, right-aligned and muted. Hints live in the status line: commands (--secondary dot), ↵ run · ↑↓ move · esc close, ○ next search 09:00 │ ? help. Below the screen: (a) the query of flattened to matches with matched letters bold, (b) kubernetes with a muted No results, (c) the letter-tile fallback for terminals without a Nerd Font.

artboards.title: Dialog
artboards.tradeoff: Calmer and closer to a launcher, but the icon tiles need a Nerd Font (letter fallback), categories are gone so ordering is suggested and recent first, and keybinds show only on the selected row, so they are less discoverable (? help lists every key)
